core_obligations: Give the categorical proof that the algebra is a colimit of finitely presented ones, and then the explicit construction: index the approximations by finite sets of generators and relations and let the transition maps be the evident inclusions (proof lines 32062-32090).
In the finite type case thin the index set to those pieces containing a fixed finite generating set, so that the transition maps become surjective (proof lines 32090-32093).
proof_roadmap: Give both the categorical and the explicit construction of the colimit (proof lines 32062-32090).
In the finite type case arrange surjective transitions (proof lines 32090-32094).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that every algebra is a directed colimit of finitely presented algebras over the base, and that in the finite type case the transition maps can be arranged to be surjective (statement lines 32054-32060). The proof gives a categorical argument and then an explicit construction indexed by finite pieces of data, and in the finite type case restricts the index set to pieces containing a fixed finite generating set so that the transitions become surjective (proof lines 32062-32094). Choosing the index set so that surjectivity comes for free is the step that settles the second assertion. H2.
